frames.narration: The application starts transaction t-77: take 20 from an account on shard A, and add 5 to one on shard B and 15 to one on shard C. It sends the coordinator the three parts and asks it to commit.
Phase one. The coordinator asks all three shards at once to prepare. Each one takes row locks, checks the change is allowed, writes a 'prepared' record to its own log and then votes.
All three vote yes. From now on each shard has promised to commit if told to, so it keeps its locks and may not abort on its own. The first phase took one round trip.

The decision. The coordinator writes 'commit t-77' to its replicated log, and a majority of the three log nodes confirm it. This is the point of no return: from this moment the transaction is committed, whatever crashes next.
The coordinator tells the application the transaction is committed, and sends commit to shard A. Then the coordinator machine dies, before shards B and C have heard anything.

Shards B and C are in doubt. They voted yes, so they cannot abort, and they keep their locks. Anyone who needs those two rows must wait. B asks shard A, which already committed, so B learns the outcome from a peer.

A standby coordinator notices the missing leader, wins an election in about three seconds and reads the replicated log. It finds 'commit t-77' with no 'end' record, so it knows exactly what is left to do.

Recovery resends commit to all three shards. A and B ignore it, because they already applied it, and C commits and releases its locks. After all three acknowledge, the log gets an 'end t-77' record. The money moved on all three shards, or on none.
